examples.ko: 두 사람은 취미가 공통돼서 금방 친해졌어요.
examples.en: The two quickly became close because they share hobbies.
These stories don't share a theme.
The two stories share a theme.

examples.ko: 두 사람 사이에 공통된 점이 하나도 없어요.
examples.en: The two have nothing in common.

examples.ko: 이 두 나라는 문화가 공통되는 부분이 많아요.
examples.en: These two countries have many parts of their culture in common.
To become friends, you need a shared topic.

explain: '비슷하다'는 모양이나 성질이 닮았다는 뜻이고, '공통되다'는 둘 이상이 함께 가진 점이 있다는 뜻이에요. '공통되는', '공통된'처럼 명사 앞에서 꾸미는 형태가 가장 많아요. '공통점', '공통으로'도 자주 써요.

phrases.en: We have a hobby in common.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸미는 형태로, 가장 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form that modifies a noun, and the most common one.

phrases.example: 두 사람의 공통점은 음악을 좋아하는 거예요.
phrases.en: What the two have in common is that they like music.
phrases.nuance_ko: 함께 가진 점을 명사로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun for the point that two or more things share.

phrases.example: 이 문제는 모든 학생에게 공통으로 나와요.
phrases.en: This question appears for all students alike.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모두에게 똑같이 해당될 때 부사처럼 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used like an adverb when something applies equally to everyone.

explain_en: '비슷하다' means looking or being alike, while '공통되다' means two or more things share something. It appears most often in the noun-modifying forms '공통되는' and '공통된'. '공통점' and '공통으로' are also common.

examples.ko: 두 분수의 공통분모를 먼저 찾아야 해요.
examples.en: You have to find the common denominator of the two fractions first.

examples.ko: 우리 세 사람의 공통분모는 영화를 좋아한다는 거예요.
examples.en: The thing the three of us have in common is that we like movies.
These songs share a common thread of sadness.

examples.ko: 공통분모가 없으면 대화가 오래 이어지기 어려워요.
examples.en: Without common ground, it's hard to keep a conversation going.
I looked into what successful people have in common.

examples.ko: 분모가 다른 분수는 공통분모로 바꿔서 더해요.
examples.en: Fractions with different denominators are converted to a common denominator before adding.

explain: 수학에서는 분수 계산에 쓰고, 일상에서는 사람이나 사물이 함께 가진 점을 비유로 말할 때 써요. 같은 뜻으로 '공통점'이 훨씬 자주 쓰이고, 공통분모는 여러 대상을 하나로 묶는 핵심이라는 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: Let's look for common ground among our different opinions.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서로 다른 것들 사이에서 함께 가진 점을 찾는다는 비유로 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used figuratively for finding what different things share.

phrases.en: The two people have nothing in common.
phrases.nuance_ko: '공통분모가 있다/없다'로 사람이나 대상이 이어지는 점이 있는지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '공통분모가 있다/없다' tells whether people or things share a connecting point.

phrases.en: The two countries have a lot in common.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻으로 일상에서 훨씬 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A much more common everyday word with a similar meaning.

explain_en: In math it is used for fractions, and in daily life it is a metaphor for what people or things share. '공통점' is much more common for the same idea, while '공통분모' feels like the key thing that ties several things together.

examples.en: Find the intersection of the two sets.
The intersection of A and B is empty.
Our tastes have almost no overlap.
The part where the two circles overlap is the intersection.
In math class we learned about intersections and unions.
I drew a picture of how big the intersection is.

explain: 반대말은 '합집합'이에요. 수학 밖에서는 취향이나 고객처럼 두 집단이 겹치는 부분을 비유로 말할 때도 '교집합이 많다/없다'라고 써요.

phrases.en: The two of us have a lot of overlap in hobbies.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수학 밖에서는 겹치는 부분이 많다는 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Outside math, used figuratively for a lot of overlap.
phrases.en_equiv: to have a lot of overlap

phrases.example: 두 모임은 사람들이 겹치지 않아서 교집합이 없어요.
phrases.en: The two groups have no overlap because their members don't coincide.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 집단이 전혀 겹치지 않을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when two groups don't overlap at all.

phrases.example: 합집합은 두 집합을 모두 합친 거예요.
phrases.en: The union is the combination of both sets.
phrases.nuance_ko: 교집합의 반대말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of '교집합'.

explain_en: Its opposite is '합집합' (union). Outside of math, people also use it figuratively for the overlap between two groups, such as tastes or customers, as in '교집합이 많다/없다'.

en: to end up as; to result in; to boil down to

examples.ko: 모든 논의는 결국 돈 문제로 귀결돼요.
examples.en: Every discussion ends up boiling down to money.
The debate ended up at the same conclusion.

examples.ko: 이 문제는 결국 교육의 질로 귀결되는 것 같아요.
examples.en: It seems this issue comes down to the quality of education.
I think all worries come down to health.
The negotiation ended without reaching an agreement.
I didn't know the story would end up like this.

explain: '~로 귀결되다'의 꼴로 쓰고, 이야기나 과정이 마지막에 하나의 결론으로 모인다는 뜻이에요. 토론이나 글에서 자주 나오고, 말할 때는 '결국 ~로 끝나다'라고 해도 돼요.

phrases.en: A small misunderstanding led to a big fight.
phrases.nuance_ko: '귀결되다'는 마지막에 하나로 모인다는 뜻이고, '이어지다'는 어떤 일이 다음 결과로 연결된다는 일상적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: '귀결되다' means everything ends up at one conclusion; '이어지다' is the everyday word for one thing leading to another.

phrases.en: The meeting ended up in a fight.
phrases.nuance_ko: '귀결되다'보다 말하기 편한 표현이라 대화에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more casual way to say 'end up as', common in conversation.

phrases.en: This argument boils down to money.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 이야기를 하나의 핵심으로 정리할 때 말로 쉽게 쓰는 꼴이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simple spoken pattern for summing up many points into one key point.

explain_en: It is used as '~로 귀결되다', meaning a discussion or process finally converges on one conclusion. It is common in debates and writing, and in speech you can say '결국 ~로 끝나다' instead.

examples.ko: 형의 조용한 성격과 동생의 활발한 성격이 대조돼요.
examples.en: The older brother's quiet nature contrasts with the younger's lively one.

examples.ko: 검은 옷이 흰 벽과 대조되어 눈에 띄었어요.
examples.en: The black clothes stood out against the white wall.

examples.ko: 두 나라의 날씨가 크게 대조된다고 해요.
examples.en: They say the weather of the two countries contrasts greatly.
The mood was quiet, in contrast to the flashy stage.
Contrasting with the first part, the story got more fun.

examples.ko: 색이 서로 대조될수록 글씨가 잘 보여요.
examples.en: The more the colors contrast, the easier the text is to read.

explain: 'A와 B가 대조되다'처럼 두 가지가 나란히 있을 때 차이가 뚜렷하게 보인다는 말이에요. 조사는 '-와/과'를 써요. 사람이 비교하는 것은 '대조하다', 저절로 차이가 드러나는 것은 '대조되다'로 구별해요.

phrases.en: The two people have contrasting personalities.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서로 많이 다른 두 가지를 설명할 때 '대조되는'을 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds '대조되는' to describe two things that differ greatly.

phrases.en: The colors of the two paintings contrast with each other.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 가지가 나란히 있어서 차이가 잘 보일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when two things side by side show a clear difference.

phrases.en: The scenery of summer and winter contrasts sharply.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차이가 아주 분명하게 보일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the difference is very clear.

explain_en: Used as 'A와 B가 대조되다': when two things sit side by side, the difference between them stands out. The particle is -와/과. A person comparing is 대조하다; differences showing up by themselves is 대조되다.

examples.ko: 수학 시간에 여러 가지 도형을 배웠어요.
examples.en: We learned about various shapes in math class.
The child is making shapes out of colored paper.
How do I find the area of this shape?
Circles and squares are the easiest shapes.

examples.ko: 칠판에 그린 도형이 잘 안 보여요.
examples.en: I can't see the shape drawn on the board well.

examples.ko: 발표 자료에 도형을 넣으면 보기 좋아요.
examples.en: Putting shapes in a presentation makes it look nice.

explain: 도형은 수학에서 쓰는 말이에요. 삼각형, 사각형, 원 같은 평면 모양이나 정육면체 같은 입체 모양을 모두 포함해요. 일상에서 물건의 모습을 말할 때는 '모양'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: Circles and triangles are plane figures.
phrases.nuance_ko: 납작한 모양을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to flat shapes.

phrases.en: A box is a solid figure.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부피가 있는 모양을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to shapes that have volume.

phrases.en: I drew various shapes in my notebook.
phrases.nuance_ko: '그리다'와 함께 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used together with 그리다.

explain_en: 도형 is a math word covering flat shapes like 삼각형, 사각형, and 원, as well as solid shapes like a cube. In everyday life, when you talk about how an object looks, you say 모양 instead.

examples.ko: 대화를 쓸 때는 따옴표를 꼭 써야 해요.
examples.en: You must use quotation marks when writing dialogue.

examples.ko: 따옴표 안에 친구가 한 말을 적으세요.
examples.en: Write what your friend said inside the quotation marks.
This sentence is missing quotation marks.
The part enclosed in quotation marks is a direct quote.

examples.ko: 소설에서는 따옴표 안에 인물의 말이 나와요.
examples.en: In novels, a character's words appear inside quotation marks.
Quotation marks come in pairs.

explain: 큰따옴표(" ")는 직접 말한 대화에, 작은따옴표(' ')는 마음속 생각이나 강조에 쓰는 게 기본이에요. 인용한 말을 표시할 때 가장 먼저 떠올리는 부호예요.

phrases.example: 직접 한 말은 큰따옴표 안에 써요.
phrases.en: Write spoken words inside double quotation marks.
phrases.nuance_ko: '따옴표' 중에서 대화나 직접 인용에 쓰는 " "만 정확히 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers specifically to the double quotation marks " " used for dialogue and direct quotes.

phrases.en: Mark inner thoughts with single quotation marks.
phrases.nuance_ko: '따옴표' 중에서 생각이나 강조에 쓰는 ' '만 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers specifically to the single quotation marks ' ' used for thoughts or emphasis.

phrases.en: I wrote my friend's words inside quotation marks.
phrases.nuance_ko: '따옴표' 뒤에 조사를 붙여 글 쓰는 위치를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase with a particle attached, used to say where text is written.

explain_en: Double quotation marks are basically for spoken dialogue, and single marks are for inner thoughts or emphasis. It is the first punctuation you think of to mark quoted words.

examples.en: The baby looks so cute dressed in a baji-jeogori outfit.
The child's baji-jeogori got covered in dirt.
I had a set of baji-jeogori made at the hanbok shop.

examples.ko: 설날에 할아버지는 바지저고리 차림으로 세배를 받으셨어요.
examples.en: On New Year's Day, my grandfather received bows dressed in baji-jeogori.
I looked at old baji-jeogori at the museum.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날 바지저고리가 흠뻑 젖어 버렸어요.
examples.en: My baji-jeogori got soaked on the rainy day.

explain: 한복의 바지와 저고리를 함께 부르는 말로, 주로 남자 한복 차림을 가리켜요. 사람에게 쓰면 줏대 없는 사람을 놀리는 말이 되니 조심하세요.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 사장님 말만 듣는 바지저고리예요.
phrases.en: a spineless person who just does as told
phrases.nuance_ko: 한복 이름이 아니라 줏대 없이 시키는 대로만 하는 사람을 놀리는 말이에요. 듣는 사람 기분이 상할 수 있어서 직접 쓰지 않는 게 좋아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Here it isn't the clothing but a teasing label for someone who has no mind of their own and just follows orders. It can offend, so avoid saying it directly to someone.

explain_en: It names the trousers and jacket of hanbok together, mostly meaning the men's outfit. When applied to a person, it becomes a teasing way to call someone spineless, so be careful.

en: level pegging; equality between two contestants

examples.ko: 두 팀의 실력은 백중지세라서 결과를 알 수 없어요.
examples.en: The two teams are evenly matched, so you can't know the result.

examples.ko: 선거 막판까지 두 후보가 백중지세를 보였어요.
examples.en: The two candidates were neck and neck until the end of the election.
The match stayed evenly balanced until the very end.

examples.ko: 두 사람의 노래 실력이 백중지세라 심사가 어려웠어요.
examples.en: The two singers were so evenly matched that judging was hard.
The scores are neck and neck, so who will win?

examples.ko: 백중지세의 싸움이라 관중들이 눈을 떼지 못했어요.
examples.en: It was such an even contest that the crowd couldn't look away.

explain: 두 상대의 실력이나 힘이 비슷해서 누가 이길지 알기 어려울 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '막상막하'를 더 많이 쓰고, '백중지세'는 뉴스나 글에서 '백중지세를 보이다, 백중지세로 이어지다'처럼 나와요.

phrases.en: The two teams were evenly matched until the end.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스나 글에서 가장 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation in news and writing.

phrases.en: The neck-and-neck match went on late into the night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 승부를 알 수 없는 싸움 앞에 붙여서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used before a contest whose winner can't be predicted.

phrases.en: The two players are equally matched.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 더 많이 쓰는 비슷한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word used more often in everyday talk.

explain_en: It is used when two opponents are so close in ability or strength that it is hard to say who will win. In everyday talk '막상막하' is more common, while '백중지세' appears in news and writing, as in '백중지세를 보이다' or '백중지세로 이어지다'.

en: to be almost equal; to have trouble telling which is better

examples.ko: 두 후보의 지지율이 백중해서 예측하기 어려워요.
examples.en: The two candidates' approval ratings are so close that it's hard to predict.
Two evenly matched players met in the final.

examples.ko: 두 팀 전력이 백중하니까 끝까지 봐야 해요.
examples.en: The two teams are evenly matched, so you have to watch to the end.
It was such a close match that I was tense until the last moment.

examples.ko: 둘의 키가 백중해서 누가 더 큰지 모르겠어요.
examples.en: They're about the same height, so I can't tell who is taller.
Our grades are always about the same.

explain: 주로 실력, 지지율, 전력처럼 서로 겨루는 대상끼리 비슷할 때 써요. 말할 때는 '막상막하예요'나 '비슷해요'도 많이 쓰고, '백중하다'는 조금 딱딱한 느낌이에요.

phrases.example: 백중한 승부 끝에 우리 팀이 이겼어요.
phrases.en: Our team won after a closely matched contest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 관형형으로 써서 승부나 실력 앞에 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in the modifier form before words like contest or skill.

phrases.example: 점수 차가 커서 두 팀은 백중하지 않아요.
phrases.en: The score gap is big, so the two teams are not evenly matched.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷하지 않다고 부정할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to deny that two sides are close.

phrases.en: The two people's singing skills are neck and neck.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때 더 자연스럽고 쉬운 비슷한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar expression that sounds more natural and easier in speech.

explain_en: It is mainly used when things that compete, such as skill, approval ratings or strength, are close to each other. In speech people also say '막상막하예요' or '비슷해요', and '백중하다' sounds a bit stiff.

en: being parallel; being in a row

examples.en: If you connect batteries in parallel, the voltage stays the same.

examples.ko: 전구를 병렬 연결하면 하나가 꺼져도 나머지는 켜져요.
examples.en: If bulbs are connected in parallel, the others stay on even if one goes out.

examples.ko: 이 두 문장은 병렬 구조로 쓰면 읽기 좋아요.
examples.en: These two sentences read well if you write them in a parallel structure.

examples.ko: 병렬 처리를 하면 컴퓨터가 더 빨리 계산해요.
examples.en: With parallel processing, a computer calculates faster.

examples.ko: 병렬이 아니라 직렬로 연결했더니 불이 어두워요.
examples.en: I connected them in series instead of in parallel, so the light is dim.
We confirmed the difference between parallel and series with an experiment.

explain: 반대말은 '직렬'이고, 전기 회로 수업에서 짝으로 가장 많이 나와요. 컴퓨터의 '병렬 처리'나 문장의 '병렬 구조'처럼 여러 개가 나란히 있는 경우에도 써요. '두 일을 병렬로 진행하다'는 동시에 한다는 뜻으로도 말해요.

phrases.example: 전구를 병렬 연결하면 각각 같은 밝기로 켜져요.
phrases.en: If you connect the bulbs in parallel, each one lights up with the same brightness.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전기 회로에서 쓰는 대표적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A representative term used for electric circuits.

phrases.en: We are doing the two tasks at the same time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일을 동시에 한다는 뜻으로 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to mean carrying out work at the same time.

phrases.en: These two sentences have a parallel structure.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문장이나 글에서 비슷한 형태가 나란히 이어질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when similar forms line up side by side in text.

explain_en: Its opposite is '직렬' (series), and the pair appears most in electric circuit lessons. It is also used when several things sit side by side, as in computer '병렬 처리' (parallel processing) or '병렬 구조' (parallel structure). '두 일을 병렬로 진행하다' means to do two tasks at the same time.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 저와 다른 부류의 사람이에요.
examples.en: That friend is a different type of person from me.
I sorted the books by category.

examples.ko: 이 문제는 두 부류로 나눌 수 있어요.
examples.en: This problem can be divided into two types.
It's comfortable when people of the same type gather.
He is the type who doesn't talk much.
Check which category it belongs to.

explain: 부류는 성질이나 특징이 비슷한 것들을 묶어서 나눈 한 무리를 가리켜요. 사람에게 쓰면 '저런 부류의 사람'처럼 약간 평가하는 느낌이 있어서 조심해서 써야 해요. 물건이나 생각을 구별할 때는 '종류'나 '유형'이 더 중립적이에요.

phrases.en: That friend and I are the same type.
phrases.nuance_ko: 성격이나 성질이 비슷한 사람끼리 묶어 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Groups people with similar character or nature.

phrases.en: I tried dividing the animals into a few categories.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 것끼리 나누어 정리한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means sorting similar things into groups.

phrases.en: There are many kinds of fruit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부류보다 평가하는 느낌이 없어서 더 편하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Has no judging feeling, so it's safer to use than 부류.

explain_en: Buryu is a group of things or people with similar traits. Used for people, as in 저런 부류의 사람, it carries a hint of judgement, so be careful. For objects and ideas, 종류 and 유형 are more neutral.

examples.ko: 두 나라 문화의 상이점을 정리해 보세요.
examples.en: Try to summarize the differences between the two countries' cultures.
The differences stand out more than the similarities.
Differences are easy to compare if you make a table.
I gave a presentation on the differences between the two products.
We should acknowledge and respect each other's differences too.

examples.ko: 상이점 몇 가지만 알면 구별할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you know just a few differences, you can tell them apart.

explain: '차이점'과 같은 뜻이지만 '상이점'이 더 딱딱해서 보고서나 발표에서 많이 써요. 반대말은 '공통점'이고, 대화에서는 '차이점'이라고 더 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: Please tell me the differences between the two languages.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻은 같지만 '상이점'보다 부드러워서 대화에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, but softer than '상이점' and more common in conversation.

phrases.example: 두 보고서의 상이점을 찾아서 표로 만들었어요.
phrases.en: I found the differences between the two reports and made a table.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비교하는 글이나 발표에서 '상이점을 찾다/정리하다'로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used as 'find/summarize the differences' in comparative writing or presentations.

phrases.example: 두 제품은 크기 말고는 큰 상이점이 없어요.
phrases.en: The two products have no big differences except for size.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차이가 거의 없다고 할 때 '상이점이 없다/적다'로 써요. 반대말은 '공통점'이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say there is little or no difference; the opposite is '공통점' (common ground).

explain_en: It means the same as '차이점' but sounds more formal, so it is common in reports and presentations. The opposite is '공통점', and in conversation people say '차이점' more often.

examples.ko: 문제를 세분하면 더 쉽게 풀 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you break the problem into parts, it is easier to solve.
We divided customers by age and sent them ads.
The grades are divided finely, so it's confusing at first.
We started by breaking the tasks down.

examples.ko: 시장을 세분할수록 필요한 게 더 잘 보여요.
examples.en: The more you divide the market, the better you see what is needed.
The fee table is divided too finely.

explain: 세분은 큰 것을 작게 나누는 일이에요. 보통 '세분하다', '세분되다'로 써서 '나누다'보다 더 잘게 나눈다는 느낌이에요. 회의나 보고서에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: We divided up the work into small parts and each took a share.
phrases.nuance_ko: '세분'의 동사형으로, 하는 사람이 있을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form of 세분, used when someone does the dividing.

phrases.en: The work is subdivided by department.
phrases.nuance_ko: 저절로, 혹은 이미 잘게 나뉘어 있는 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a state that is already divided into small parts.

phrases.en: If you break homework into small pieces, it's much easier.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '세분하다' 대신 쓸 수 있는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy everyday alternative to 세분하다.

explain_en: 세분 is dividing something large into fine parts. It is usually used as 세분하다 or 세분되다 and feels finer than 나누다. It often appears in meetings and reports.

en: positive pole; both poles; two extremes

examples.ko: 건전지의 양극과 음극을 맞춰 끼워야 해요.
examples.en: You have to insert the battery with the positive and negative ends matched.

examples.ko: 배터리 양극에 문제가 생겨서 전원이 안 켜져요.
examples.en: There is a problem with the battery's positive terminal, so it won't turn on.
I'm worried because income polarization is serious these days.

examples.ko: 자석의 양극은 서로 다른 극끼리 끌어당겨요.
examples.en: The two poles of a magnet attract each other when they are different.
The Earth's two poles are the North Pole and the South Pole.
People's opinions split into two extremes.

explain: '양극'은 전기에서 + 쪽 극(陽極)을 말하기도 하고, 지구나 자석의 두 끝(兩極)이나 정반대의 두 입장을 말하기도 해요. 전기에서 반대말은 '음극'이고, '양극화'는 두 끝으로 갈라지는 것을 뜻해서 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The gap between rich and poor is getting more extreme.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 두 쪽으로 크게 갈라지는 현상을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in the news for splitting into two opposite extremes.

phrases.en: A battery's positive pole is +, and the negative pole is -.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전기에서 '양극'의 반대말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 양극 in electricity.

phrases.example: 이 문제는 사람들 의견이 양극으로 갈려요.
phrases.en: People's opinions on this issue split into two extremes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 의견이 정반대의 두 쪽으로 나뉠 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when opinions divide into two opposite sides.

explain_en: '양극' can mean the positive electrode (陽極) in electricity, or the two ends (兩極) of the Earth or a magnet, or two opposite positions. In electricity the opposite is '음극', and '양극화' (polarization), meaning splitting into two extremes, often appears in the news.

en: to be all of a sort

examples.en: The prices at the two shops are about the same.
Those singers' voices are so alike that I mix them up.

examples.ko: 어슷비슷한 디자인이 너무 많아서 고르기 어려워요.
examples.en: There are so many similar designs that it's hard to choose.
Their ages and heights are so alike that they look like brothers.
The candidates' pledges are all pretty much the same.
The two people's scores came out about even.

explain: '비슷하다'보다 큰 차이가 없이 다 거기서 거기라는 느낌이 강해요. 고르거나 비교할 때 '이것도 저것도 별 차이 없다'고 말하는 상황에 잘 어울려요. '고만고만하다'와도 비슷하게 쓰여요.

phrases.en: Everyone on our team has about the same skill.
phrases.nuance_ko: 큰 차이 없이 거의 같은 수준을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes levels that are almost the same, with no big gap.

phrases.en: The twins look quite alike.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습이 거기서 거기일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when appearances are all about the same.

phrases.en: The prices are about the same at every shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: '어슷비슷하다'와 비슷하게 별 차이가 없다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 어슷비슷하다, meaning there is little difference.

explain_en: Compared with '비슷하다', it strongly suggests that things are all about the same with no big difference. It fits situations where you choose or compare and say there is little difference between this and that. It is also used much like '고만고만하다'.

examples.en: The two teams traded the lead back and forth.

examples.ko: 어젯밤에는 걱정돼서 엎치락뒤치락 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: I was worried last night and tossed and turned without sleeping.
The kids rolled around playing on the bed.
First and second place kept swapping ranks.

examples.ko: 요즘 인기 순위가 엎치락뒤치락 계속 바뀌어요.
examples.en: The popularity rankings keep flipping back and forth these days.

examples.ko: 선거 결과는 엎치락뒤치락 끝까지 알 수 없었어요.
examples.en: The election was so back and forth that we couldn't know the result until the end.

explain: 뒤집히고 바뀌는 모습을 나타내서, 경기나 순위에서 서로 앞서거니 뒤서거니 할 때와 잠을 못 자고 이리저리 뒤척일 때 둘 다 써요. 동작을 말할 때는 '엎치락뒤치락하다'로도 써요.

phrases.en: The kids tumbled and fought on the floor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서로 뒤엉켜 위아래가 바뀌는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes people tangled up and swapping top and bottom positions.

phrases.en: The rankings kept flipping throughout the competition.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서로 앞서거니 뒤서거니 하는 접전에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a close race where the lead keeps changing.

phrases.en: The two candidates keep trading the lead.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부사 '엎치락뒤치락'에 '하다'를 붙인 동사형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form made by adding '하다' to the adverb.

explain_en: It shows things flipping and swapping, so it is used both when competitors keep overtaking each other in a game or ranking and when someone tosses and turns unable to sleep. As an action it also appears as '엎치락뒤치락하다'.

examples.en: The main ingredients of this snack are flour and sugar.
Check the main ingredient of the medicine before taking it.

examples.ko: 이 비누는 천연 오일을 주성분으로 해요.
examples.en: This soap is made mainly from natural oil.

examples.ko: 두 제품은 주성분이 같아서 효과도 비슷해요.
examples.en: The two products have the same main ingredient, so the effect is similar.

examples.ko: 주성분 외에 다른 첨가물도 들어 있어요.
examples.en: Besides the main ingredient, there are other additives too.
The main ingredient differs a little from cold medicine to cold medicine.

explain: 음식을 만들 때는 '주재료'를 더 많이 말하고, '주성분'은 약, 화장품, 비누, 과자처럼 제품에 들어 있는 핵심 물질을 말할 때 써요. 제품 뒷면의 설명이나 설명서에서 자주 보여요. 과학에서는 어떤 물질을 이루는 가장 중요한 성분이라는 뜻으로도 나와요.

phrases.en: Check the main ingredient before you take the medicine.
phrases.nuance_ko: 약이나 화장품을 쓰기 전에 핵심 물질을 살펴볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when checking the key substance before using a medicine or cosmetic.

phrases.en: What are the main ingredients of this medicine?
phrases.nuance_ko: '주성분'과 비슷하고 여러 성분을 함께 물을 때 편해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '주성분', handy when asking about several ingredients.

phrases.en: The main ingredients of gimbap are rice and seaweed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식을 만들 때 쓰는 주된 재료는 '주재료'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: For the main food items used in cooking, say '주재료'.

explain_en: When cooking people say '주재료' more often, while '주성분' is for the key substance in products such as medicine, cosmetics, soap and snacks. You often see it in the text on the back of products or in instructions. In science it also means the most important component of a substance.

en: to integrate; to unify; to consolidate

examples.en: We merge the two teams into one.
The company merged several sites.
Merging the data is difficult.
Please tell me how to merge the files.
We integrate and manage the services.
I want to integrate all the records.

explain: '합치다'는 일상에서 쓰고, '통합하다'는 조직이나 시스템처럼 큰 것을 하나로 묶을 때 써요. 일하는 곳에서 자주 들어요. 목적어에 '를/을'을 붙여 '무엇을 통합하다'로 써요.

phrases.en: I combine the two files into one.
phrases.nuance_ko: '통합하다'보다 쉽고 일상에서 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier and more everyday than 통합하다.

phrases.en: I want to merge the accounts into one.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바라는 일을 말할 때 '-고 싶다'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds -고 싶다 to express what you want to do.

phrases.en: Please merge these two lists.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일터에서 부탁할 때 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common way to make a request at work.

explain_en: The everyday verb for putting things together is casual; this one fits larger things like organizations and systems and is often heard at work. It takes an object, as in 'integrate something'.
